title: Coalition-Formation Outcomes — Nordic + DACH 2010–2024
description: Base-rate dataset recording government coalition formation outcomes in Nordic countries (Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland) and DACH countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland) from 2010 to 2024. Provides empirical priors for coalition-scenario probability assignments, SD compliance rates, incumbent-retention forecasts, and grand-coalition base rates.
authority: ICD 203 §3.2 — base-rate anchoring; Heuer & Pherson SAT (3rd ed.) ch. 8; Comparative Constitutional Design (Ginsburg et al. 2012)

primary_sources.name: Parliamentary Affairs journal — Nordic coalition studies (Bergman et al.)
primary_sources.notes: Peer-reviewed aggregate data on Nordic coalition formation

methodology: All government formations in the 7 covered countries from 2010-01-01 to 2024-12-31, coded by: (a) bloc outcome (incumbent-retained / bloc-switch / grand-coalition), (b) minority vs. majority, (c) confidence-and-supply vs. formal coalition. Sweden-specific: SD compliance rate measured as % of chamber votes where SD voted Ja or Frånvarande (abstain supportive) on government propositions during confidence-and-supply agreement.

aggregate_rates.nordic_coalition_quarterly_survival_rate: Proportion of Nordic governments surviving any given quarter (quarterly granularity, N=320 quarters across 4 Nordic countries 2010–2024)
aggregate_rates.nordic_incumbent_retention_rate_note: Proportion of Nordic elections where the incumbent government coalition is returned to power (N=18 Nordic elections 2010–2024)
aggregate_rates.sweden_budget_pass_first_vote_rate_note: Proportion of Swedish budgetramverk first-chamber votes passing without minority amendment (N=14 votes 2010–2024)
aggregate_rates.sweden_left_bloc_minority_formation_rate: S-led bloc minority government formations out of all post-2010 Swedish government formations (N=5 formations)
aggregate_rates.sweden_left_bloc_majority_rate_note: S-led bloc achieving ≥175 seats in Riksdag election (N=4 elections 2010–2022; 2024 Demoskop model-based extrapolation)
aggregate_rates.nordic_grand_coalition_formation_rate_no: Cross-bloc grand-coalition formations in Nordic countries (extremely rare; N=1 instance in all 4 countries 2010–2024)
aggregate_rates.sd_confidence_supply_compliance_rate_not: SD compliance on government votes during 2022–2024 confidence-and-supply agreement: % of chamber votes where SD did not defect (N=1547 votes)
aggregate_rates.eu_state_aid_review_opening_rate_note: Proportion of Nordic fiscal measures subject to EU formal state-aid review within 6 months of adoption (N=78 Nordic fiscal measures 2010–2024; EC state-aid register)
aggregate_rates.eu_edp_opening_sweden_rate_note: Probability of Sweden entering EU EDP in any given calendar year, based on fiscal trajectory (N=12 Swedish years 2010–2021; current structural balance well above -3% threshold)

sweden_government_formations.collapse_note: Budget lost December 2014; snap election avoided via Decemberöverenskommelsen

sweden_government_formations.government: Löfven II (S+MP minority; Januariavtalet with C+L)
sweden_government_formations.collapse_note: Lost confidence vote June 2021; reinstated after SP negotiations

dach_summary.note: CDU/CSU+SPD grand coalitions in 2013 and 2017; SPD+FDP+Grüne 2021
Swiss Federal Council is a permanent grand coalition (Zauberformel) — excluded from Nordic base-rate calculations

calibration_notes: Nordic base rates are more relevant than DACH for Swedish coalition forecasts due to institutional similarity
Sweden's SD confidence-and-supply arrangement is structurally novel (no Nordic precedent pre-2022); compliance rate of 91% based on actual vote records 2022–2024
Incumbent retention rate of 41% is mean across 4 Nordic countries; Sweden's own rate is 50% (2 of 4 elections); use Swedish-specific where precision matters
Grand coalition (M+S equivalent) has zero Nordic precedents 2010–2024; base rate drawn from DACH analogues yields ~3% prior
EU state-aid review opening rate of 14% is across all Nordic fiscal measures; fuel-tax cuts specifically may have higher rate — elevate to 20% when domain is energy/fuel subsidy
